Fresh Batch 0059 unread-message isolated source-first re-review

claims.text: The frozen source contains both 500k-QPS and 500k-OPS unread-message variants but no production traffic mix or per-node capacity; the candidate separates list/count reads, message ingest, fanout writes and read-state writes and treats 500k as a target to prove from measured safe per-shard throughput plus headroom.

Redis Cluster provides key-level hash-slot sharding and sorted sets can provide an ordered per-recipient hot index, but Redis Cluster and WAIT do not provide an unqualified strong-consistency/lossless fact store; the candidate therefore keeps durable message, delivery and read-state facts separate from rebuildable Redis materialization.

Asynchronous fanout is replayable and its delivery side effect is idempotent per event plus recipient; acknowledgement or checkpoint advancement follows a successful or durably recoverable side effect so retries and worker failure cannot permanently lose or duplicate logical deliveries.

The candidate models read state as monotonic cursor/version state where applicable and treats unread count/index as repairable materialization; duplicates, late events, mark-read races and rebuild replay are prevented from permanently double-counting or resurrecting messages by uniqueness, monotonicity and reconciliation invariants.

Recipient-key sharding localizes the dominant inbox read path but one user key still maps to one Redis slot, so hot-user skew remains; the candidate separates targeted fanout from high-fanout broadcasts and offers shared broadcast/topic state plus cursor/segment materialization instead of synchronous O(all users) fanout.

The candidate requires latency/throughput, queue lag and oldest-event age, retry/pending, Redis hit/skew, durable-store latency, unread drift and rebuild metrics, and requires target-environment mixed-load, hot-key, failover and backlog-recovery tests before claiming the 500k target is proven; it does not fabricate production topology or metrics.

findings: The frozen repository context preserves both 500k-QPS and 500k-OPS unread-message variants plus the recipient/inverted-index, sharded-storage, high-concurrency and Redis concerns; the revised candidate keeps QPS and OPS as separate workload dimensions instead of silently normalizing them into one number.

The frozen primary-source packet supports Redis Cluster hash-slot and write-safety boundaries, sorted-set ordered indexing, Streams acknowledgement/recovery semantics, WAIT's non-strong-consistency boundary and Kafka partition/replication scaling; the candidate does not turn those primitives into an unsupported single-node capacity claim.

The scenario answer defines durable message/delivery/read-state facts, recipient-oriented materialization, targeted versus broadcast fanout, replay/idempotency, monotonic read-state repair, hot-key skew handling, reconciliation, observability, target-environment capacity proof and failure/backlog recovery, so it satisfies the scenario-specific data-flow, consistency, capacity and operability requirements.

The revision only normalizes the seven question-specific followups into the repository's machine-auditable '- 问：' syntax; their semantics remain specific to Redis durability, database fallback, broadcast fanout, replay, unread-count correctness, WAIT and 500k capacity proof.

The candidate states that 500k is a target requiring measurement, separates Redis materialization from durable truth, does not claim Redis Cluster or WAIT is strongly consistent, and does not fabricate company topology, production metrics, node counts, incidents or personal project history.

The one-minute section still uses six numbered beats rather than the content standard's preferred three-to-five main points; it remains coherent and non-blocking, so oral_quality is 4/5 rather than 5/5.
